title: Biased AI improves human performance but reduces perceived helpfulness
abstract: arXiv:2508.09297v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly shapes how people think, engage, and evaluate information. To minimize risk, most current systems are designed to present as ideologically neutral with standardized output. Yet growing evidence suggests that these principles suppress cognitive engagement, impair human decision-making, and erode societal diversity. Here we test the opposite approach by deliberately injecting bias into AI assistants. In three randomized experiments with 5,000 participants, biased AI improved human performance relative to default and neutral AI in tasks ranging from misinformation evaluation and financial investment to graduate education. These gains carried a subjective cost. Participants systematically undervalued AI they believed to be biased and inflated the helpfulness of AI they believed to be neutral, regardless of the systems' actual behavior. translated_title: 有偏见的AI能提升人类表现，但会降低其被感知的有用性
translated_abstract: 人工智能（AI）日益影响着人们的思考、参与和信息评估方式。为了降低风险，目前大多数系统被设计成在意识形态上保持中立、输出标准化的形式。然而，越来越多的证据表明，这些原则抑制了认知参与，损害了人类决策，并削弱了社会多样性。在此，我们通过有意向AI助手注入偏见来检验相反的方法。在三项共5,000名参与者参与的随机实验中，有偏见的AI在从虚假信息评估、金融投资到研究生教育等任务中，相比默认和中立的AI提升了人类的表现。但这些收益伴随着主观代价：无论系统的实际行为如何，参与者系统性地低估他们认为有偏见的AI，并高估他们认为中立的AI的有用性。当与两个偏见分别位于参与者自身立场两侧的AI互动时……
tldr: 研究通过5,000人的随机实验发现，故意注入偏见的有偏AI能显著提升人类在虚假信息评估、金融投资等任务中的表现，但用户却系统性地低估这类AI的有用性，反而高估实际帮助较小的中立AI。
en_tdlr: Deliberately biased AI improves human performance across tasks such as misinformation evaluation and financial investment, yet users systematically undervalue it and overestimate the helpfulness of neutral AI regardless of actual behavior.
